classification.difficultyReason: Part a needs the base diagonal, then half of it, then tan⁻¹ to find the angle of the edge with the base. Part b needs the midpoint-to-centre distance as half of the other side. Both are fairly short chains, but the student has to choose the right base distance.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the angle between the sloping edge $EC$ and the base, to the nearest degree.

children.label: b
children.prompt: $M$ is the midpoint of $BC$. Find the angle between the apothem $EM$ and the base, to the nearest degree.

answer.worked:
$O$ is the centre of the base, so $OM$ is half of $DC$: $OM=18\div2=9\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}\tan\angle EMO&=\frac{7}{9}\\\angle EMO&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{7}{9}\right)\\&\approx38^\circ\end{align*}$$
